question: In a past-life tale, a crow decides it can fish for itself instead of sharing a water-bird's catch, and gets tangled in the weeds. Which story contains it?
title: The Story about the Young Sow
synopsis: One day the Buddha saw a sow and smiled; when Elder Ānanda asked him the reason for his smile he told of the various forms of existence that the sow had been through, including being reborn in the Brahma worlds in the life before this one; he then taught the monastics on the wickedness of craving with some verses. verse_english: Dhp 338: A tree grows back even when cut down, so long as its roots are strong and undamaged; suffering springs up again and again, so long as the tendency to craving is not pulled out. / Dhp 339: A person of low views in whom the thirty-six streams that flow to pleasure are mighty, is swept away by lustful thoughts. / Dhp 340: The streams flow everywhere; a weed springs up and remains. Seeing this weed that has been born, cut the root with wisdom. / Dhp 341: A personage’s joys flow from senses and cravings. Seekers of happiness, bent on pleasure, continue to be reborn and grow old. / Dhp 342: People governed by thirst, crawl about like a trapped rabbit. Bound and fettered, for a long time they return to pain time and again. / Dhp 343: People governed by thirst, crawl about like a trapped rabbit. That’s why one who longs for dispassion should dispel thirst.

title: The Story about Culla Sāri
synopsis: Elder Culla Sāri gave medical treatment to others in exchange for a portion of food, which is against the right ways of earning his livelihood as laid down by the Buddha; when the Buddha heard of his behaviour he gave a teaching in some verses.
verse_english: Dhp 244: Life is easy for the shameless. With all the rude courage of a crow, they live pushy, rude, and corrupt. / Dhp 245: Life is hard for the conscientious, always seeking purity, neither clinging nor rude, pure of livelihood and discerning.

question: In a past-life tale, a crow decides it can fish for itself instead of sharing a water-bird's catch, and gets tangled in the weeds. Which story contains it?
title: The Story about a Company of Old Elders
synopsis: Some laymen heard the Buddha teaching and ordained in old age, but even after ordaining they still visited their families for meals; when a former wife of one of them died they fell into deep lamentation; the Buddha explained they did that also in previous lives as crows, and gave the bhikkhus a teaching with some verses.
verse_english: Dhp 283: Cut down the jungle, not just a tree; from the jungle springs fear. Having cut down jungle and snarl, be free of jungles, mendicants! / Dhp 284: So long as the vine, no matter how small, that ties a man to women is not cut, his mind remains trapped, like a calf suckling its mother.

question: In a past-life tale, a crow decides it can fish for itself instead of sharing a water-bird's catch, and gets tangled in the weeds. Which story contains it?
title: The Story about Devadatta
synopsis: Devadatta grew jealous and plotted to kill the Buddha, when that failed he tried to cause a schism; eventually he wished to seek for forgiveness, but before he reached the Buddha he fell into Avīci, the hell of relentless suffering; the Buddha summarised the events with a verse. verse_english: Dhp 17: Here they’re tormented, hereafter they’re tormented, an evildoer is tormented in both places. They’re tormented thinking of bad things they’ve done; when gone to a bad place, they’re tormented all the more.

question: In a past-life tale, a crow decides it can fish for itself instead of sharing a water-bird's catch, and gets tangled in the weeds. Which story contains it?
title: The Story about Aṅkura
synopsis: Aṅkura was a good Brahmin who set up many fire places and worshipped the gods for ten thousand years, yet his position in the heavens was less than Indaka who gave just one spoonful of rice to Elder Anuruddha; the Buddha explained with some verses that one should give with discrimination, as gifts given to those who are free of defilements yield great fruit.
verse_english: Dhp 356: Weeds are the bane of crops, but greed is these folk’s bane. That’s why a gift to one rid of greed is so very fruitful. / Dhp 357: Weeds are the bane of crops, but hate is these folk’s bane. That’s why a gift to one rid of hate is so very fruitful. / Dhp 358: Weeds are the bane of crops, but delusion is these folk’s bane. That’s why a gift to one rid of delusion is so very fruitful. / Dhp 359: Weeds are the bane of crops, but desire is these folk’s bane. That’s why a gift to one rid of desire is so very fruitful.

question: In a past-life tale, a crow decides it can fish for itself instead of sharing a water-bird's catch, and gets tangled in the weeds. Which story contains it?
title: The Story about Three Groups
synopsis: Three different groups of bhikkhus who were on their way to the Buddha saw a crow die in mid-air, a woman drowned on a voyage and themselves get buried in a cave; they asked the Buddha why it all happened, and he explained there is nowhere to escape from the results of bad actions, and spoke a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 127: Not in midair, nor mid-ocean, nor hiding in a mountain cleft; you’ll find no place on the planet to escape your wicked deeds.

question: In a past-life tale, a crow decides it can fish for itself instead of sharing a water-bird's catch, and gets tangled in the weeds. Which story contains it?
title: The Story about the Elder Upananda the Sakyan
synopsis: Elder Upananda taught well, but was a greedy bhikkhu who always took the biggest offering, one day he swindled two bhikkhus out of a blanket, and the Buddha explained that one should train oneself before teaching to others, and summarised his teaching with a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 158: The astute would avoid being corrupted by first grounding themselves in what is suitable, and then instructing others.

question: Which monk daydreamed about selling a robe to buy a goat, starting a family, and then losing the baby under a cart wheel?
title: The Story about Devadatta
synopsis: Elder Sāriputta taught on generosity and people decided to give alms; one man gave a robe, which they decided to give to Elder Devadatta; when the Buddha heard about it he related a Birth Story about Devadatta, who, as an elephant hunter, disguised himself as a Paccekabuddha in order to kill his prey, and then spoke some verses about him.
verse_english: Dhp 9: One who, not free of stains themselves, would wear the robe stained in ocher, bereft of self-control and truth: they are not worthy of the ocher robe. / Dhp 10: One who’s purged all their stains, steady in ethics, possessed of self-control and of truth, they are truly worthy of the ocher robe.

question: Which monk daydreamed about selling a robe to buy a goat, starting a family, and then losing the baby under a cart wheel?
title: The Story about the Elder Cittahattha
synopsis: Cittahattha wavered continually between being a bhikkhu and a householder, but eventually he saw into the truth of impermanence, ordained yet again and became an Arahat; the Buddha spoke some verses about him.
verse_english: Dhp 38: Those of unsteady mind, who don’t understand the true teaching, and whose confidence wavers, do not perfect their wisdom. / Dhp 39: One whose mind is not festering, whose heart is undamaged, who’s given up right and wrong, alert, has nothing to fear.

question: Which monk daydreamed about selling a robe to buy a goat, starting a family, and then losing the baby under a cart wheel?
title: The Story about a Certain Bhikkhu
synopsis: A bhikkhu was given a meditation subject but could make no progress, so he determined to return to the Buddha; on his way he saw a great fire burn down a forest, and the Buddha appeared to him and taught him with a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 31: A mendicant who loves diligence, seeing fear in negligence— advances like fire, burning up fetters big and small.

title: The Story about Nephew Saṅgharakkhita
synopsis: Saṅgharakkhita ordained as a bhikkhu and received robes, one of which he wished to give to an elder, his uncle; the elder had no need for it though and refused it; Elder Saṅgharakkhita daydreamed about returning to the household life, and was distressed when his daydream was exposed, and the Buddha taught him in a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 37: The mind travels far, wandering alone; incorporeal, it lies hidden in the heart. Those who will restrain the mind are freed from Māra’s bonds.

title: The Story about the Elder Nanda
synopsis: The Buddha’s half-brother Nanda ordained, but yearned for the lay-life; the Buddha promised him celestial maidens as a reward for his efforts in the spiritual life; Nanda put forth effort and became an Arahat, and the Buddha was released from his promise; these verses were spoken about him. Lives
verse_english: Dhp 13: Just as rain seeps into a poorly roofed house, lust seeps into an undeveloped mind. / Dhp 14: Just as rain doesn’t seep into a well roofed house, lust doesn’t seep into a well developed mind.

question: Which monk daydreamed about selling a robe to buy a goat, starting a family, and then losing the baby under a cart wheel?
title: The Story about the Fruits and Powers of People’s Bad Conduct
synopsis: Elder Moggallāna saw a Peta dressed as a bhikkhu flying through the air with body all on fire and reported it to the Buddha, who told that previously the Peta had been a bhikkhu under Buddha Kassapa, but had not lived accordingly, and then he spoke a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 307: Many who wear a scrap of ocher cloth are unrestrained and wicked. Being wicked, they are reborn in hell due to their bad deeds.

question: A woman tells a visiting old friend that she is actually the young man who vanished years ago on the way to bathe. Which story is this?
title: The Story about the One Who Honoured Her Husband
synopsis: Patipūjikā passed away from heaven and was reborn on earth, had four sons, served the monastics faithfully, and at the end of her life was reunited with her husband Mālabhārī in Tāvatiṁsa Heaven; the monastics told the Buddha about the loss of their benefactor, and he gave this teaching.
verse_english: Dhp 48: The terminator gains control of the man who has not had his fill of pleasures, even as he gathers flowers, his mind caught up in them.

title: The Story about the Young Brahmin Girl Ciñcā
synopsis: The young brahmin girl Ciñcā falsely accused the Buddha of impregnating her; the gods helped reveal the lie, and Ciñcā fell into Avīci, the hell of relentless suffering; the Buddha explained the matter with a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 176: When a personage, spurning the hereafter, transgresses in just one thing— lying— there is no evil they would not do.

question: A woman tells a visiting old friend that she is actually the young man who vanished years ago on the way to bathe. Which story is this?
title: The Story about Nandiya
synopsis: The faithful householder Nandiya erected a building at Isipatana for the monastics and as he poured the water of donation a celestial mansion arose for him in the Realm of the Thirty-Three gods; Elder Moggallāna saw it and asked the Buddha about it, who explained the matter with a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 219: When a man returns safely after a long time spent abroad, family, friends, and loved ones celebrate his return. / Dhp 220: Just so, when one who has done good goes from this world to the next, their good deeds receive them there, as family welcomes home one they love.

title: The Story about the Elder Mahā Kassapa’s Pupil
synopsis: A faithless pupil of Elder Mahā Kassapa, after numerous other acts of deceit, tricked a supporter into giving him food and drinks which he said were needed by the elder; after being rebuked he burned down the elder’s hut, ran away and was later reborn in Avīci, the relentless hell; the Buddha then gave some advice in verse.
verse_english: Dhp 61: If while wandering you find no partner equal or better than yourself, then firmly resolve to wander alone— there’s no fellowship with fools.

question: A woman tells a visiting old friend that she is actually the young man who vanished years ago on the way to bathe. Which story is this?
title: The Story about the Yakkhinī Kāḷi
synopsis: A barren woman brings home a young woman for her husband, but every time the young wife conceives the barren wife contrives an abortion; through life after life they consume each other’s children, until brought to the Buddha, who taught them with a verse. named, Elder Ānanda, Deva Sumana
verse_english: Dhp 5: For never is hatred laid to rest by hate, it’s laid to rest by love: this is an ancient teaching.

question: A woman tells a visiting old friend that she is actually the young man who vanished years ago on the way to bathe. Which story is this?
title: The Story about the Elder Soreyya
synopsis: A merchant’s son, Soreyya, developed lust for Elder Mahā Kaccāyana and was transformed into a woman; later, after asking pardon, he became a man again, ordained and soon became an Arahat; the Buddha explained what a well-directed mind can do for one.
verse_english: Dhp 43: A rightly directed mind would do you more good than your mother or father or any other relative.

question: A woman tells a visiting old friend that she is actually the young man who vanished years ago on the way to bathe. Which story is this?
title: The Story about a Certain Youth of Good Family
synopsis: A youth got married but his wife was given to adultery and put the young man to shame; when he met the Buddha the latter reminded him that in a previous existence also he was betrayed by his wife, and then he taught him with a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 242: Misconduct is a woman’s stain. A giver’s stain is stinginess. Bad qualities are a stain in this world and the next. / Dhp 243: But a worse stain than these is ignorance, the worst stain of all. Having given up that stain, be without stains, mendicants!

question: A woman tells a visiting old friend that she is actually the young man who vanished years ago on the way to bathe. Which story is this?
title: The Story about a Woman Who Ate Chicken Eggs
synopsis: A young girl stole a hen’s eggs, and the hen, when reborn killed the girl’s offspring; through their hateful connection they were reborn together and destroyed each other’s children in five hundred existences; when the Buddha met them he taught them with a verse, and their hatreds were appeased.
verse_english: Dhp 291: Seeking their own happiness by imposing suffering on others, intimate with enmity, they’re not freed from enmity.

verse_english: Dhp 47: As a mighty flood sweeps off a sleeping village, death steals away a man even as he gathers flowers, his mind caught up in them.

title: The Story about the Mother of Kāṇā
synopsis: Kāṇā resented and reviled the bhikkhus for taking cakes she wanted to offer to her husband; but the Buddha showed they had only taken what was offered, and she gained faith and attained Stream-entry; the Buddha explained she had also been offended in a past life, and then spoke a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 82: Like a deep lake, clear and unclouded, so clear are the astute when they hear the teachings.

verse_english: Dhp 181: The attentive intent on absorption, who love the peace of renunciation, the Buddhas, ever mindful, are envied by even the gods.

title: The Story about the Old Brahmin’s Sons
synopsis: Some children who were previously negligent later gave a meal to the Buddha and the Saṅgha, and related how they now took care of their father; the Buddha recited a Birth Story relating how he too had cared for his parents, and spoke a verse showing how he would not eat until he was allowed to attend to his duties.
verse_english: Dhp 324: The tusker named Dhanapāla is musky in rut, hard to control. Bound, he eats not a morsel, for he misses the elephant forest.

title: The Story about the Elder Candābha
synopsis: Because of a past deed a light shone from the torso of the boy Candābha and he was taken round the country giving blessings; when he entered into the presence of the Buddha, however, the light disappeared; he then ordained and soon became an Arahat; the bhikkhus doubted his attainment and asked the Buddha, who spoke a verse about him.
verse_english: Dhp 413: Pure as the spotless moon, clear and undisturbed, they’ve ended relish for rebirth: that’s who I declare a brahmin.

title: The Story about the Prison House
synopsis: Some bhikkhus while on almsround saw various criminals in the prison house where they were bound with ropes and chains; they reported it to the Buddha who explained that these bonds are paltry compared to the bonds of craving, and he taught them further with some verses.
verse_english: Dhp 345: The attentive say that shackle is not strong that’s made of iron, wood, or knots. But obsession with jeweled earrings, concern for your partners and children: / Dhp 346: this, say the attentive, is a strong shackle dragging the indulgent down, hard to escape. Having cut this one too they go forth, unconcerned, having given up sensual pleasures.

title: The Story about the Lay Disciple Mahā Kāla
synopsis: The householder Mahā Kāla listened to an all-night Dhamma teaching at Jetavana, but in the morning was beaten to death by people who mistook him for a thief; the Buddha explained that he had caused the unjust death of another in a previous life, and his bad deed had caught up with him, and gave a teaching in a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 161: For the evil that is done by oneself, born and produced in oneself, grinds down a simpleton, as diamond grinds a lesser gem.

question: A ruler brings soldiers to a monk's room after dark, hunting for a female companion people had complained about, and finds nobody. Which story?

verse_english: Dhp 6: When others do not understand, let us, who do understand this, restrain ourselves in this regard; for that is how conflicts are laid to rest.

Buddhas
verse_english: Dhp 133: Don’t speak harshly, they may speak harshly back. For aggressive speech is painful, and the rod may spring back on you. / Dhp 134: If you still yourself like a broken gong, you reach extinguishment and know no conflict.

question: A ruler brings soldiers to a monk's room after dark, hunting for a female companion people had complained about, and finds nobody. Which story?

synopsis: Queen Māgandiyā, who had been rejected by the Buddha, bribed the crowd and slaves to abuse him and the bhikkhus when they came to town; Elder Ānanda urged the Buddha to go elsewhere but the Buddha answered that they should be resolute and spoke about himself in these verses.
verse_english: Dhp 320: Like an elephant struck with arrows in battle, I shall endure abuse, for so many folk are badly behaved. / Dhp 321: The well-tamed beast is the one led to the crowd; the tamed elephant’s the one the king mounts; the tamed person who endures abuse is the best of human beings. / Dhp 322: Those who have tamed themselves are better than fine tamed mules, thoroughbreds from Sindh, or giant tuskers.

synopsis: Owing to the Kosambī bhikkhus falling into an argument, the Buddha went to Pārileyyaka forest and was served by an elephant; after the Rains Retreat Elder Ānanda, being urged by the great disciples, went to invite the Buddha to return to Sāvatthi; the Buddha explained that he had a good companion in the elephant, but without such-like it is better to live alone, and he spoke some verses.
verse_english: Dhp 328: If you find an alert companion, an attentive friend to live happily together, then, overcoming all adversities, wander with them, joyful and mindful. / Dhp 329: If you find no alert companion, no attentive friend to live happily together, then, like a king who flees his conquered realm, wander alone like a tusker in the wilds. / Dhp 330: It’s better to wander alone, there’s no fellowship with fools. question: A ruler brings soldiers to a monk's room after dark, hunting for a female companion people had complained about, and finds nobody. Which story?
title: The Story about the Bhikkhus Who Lived on the Banks of the Vaggumudā
synopsis: The bhikkhus who lived on the banks of the Vaggumudā went around praising each other and saying they had attained states they had not in order to get better almsfood; the Buddha restrained those bhikkhus and spoke a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 308: It’d be better for the immoral and unrestrained to eat an iron ball, scorching, like a burning flame, than to eat the nation’s alms.

question: In one past-life story a couple are the only survivors when their boat goes down, and they end up stranded, eating whatever the local birds lay. Which story?
title: The Story about Prince Bodhi
synopsis: Prince Bodhi invited the Buddha for the first meal in his new palace, and put down cloth thinking if the Buddha stepped on it he would be blessed with children; the Buddha refused to walk on it, and explained that Prince Bodhi would be without children because of a past life in which he failed to protect himself by keeping precepts during any of the three periods of his life, and he then gave a teaching in a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 157: If you knew your self as beloved, you’d look after it so well. In one of the night’s three watches, an astute person would remain alert.

question: In one past-life story a couple are the only survivors when their boat goes down, and they end up stranded, eating whatever the local birds lay. Which story?
title: The Story about the Prison House
synopsis: Some bhikkhus while on almsround saw various criminals in the prison house where they were bound with ropes and chains; they reported it to the Buddha who explained that these bonds are paltry compared to the bonds of craving, and he taught them further with some verses.
verse_english: Dhp 345: The attentive say that shackle is not strong that’s made of iron, wood, or knots. But obsession with jeweled earrings, concern for your partners and children: / Dhp 346: this, say the attentive, is a strong shackle dragging the indulgent down, hard to escape. Having cut this one too they go forth, unconcerned, having given up sensual pleasures.

question: In one past-life story a couple are the only survivors when their boat goes down, and they end up stranded, eating whatever the local birds lay. Which story?
title: The Story about a Company of Bhikkhus
synopsis: After Soṇa Kūṭikaṇṇa received ordination he recited Dhamma to the Buddha who praised him for it, which also caused the Devas to rejoice; on hearing about it, Soṇa’s mother invited her son to teach her Dhamma also, and wouldn’t leave the teaching even when she heard nine hundred thieves had broken into her house; seeing her piety, the thieves converted and went forth; this is the teaching the Buddha gave at that time.
verse_english: Dhp 368: A mendicant who meditates on love, devoted to the Buddha’s teaching, would realize the peaceful state, the blissful stilling of conditions. / Dhp 369: Bail out this boat, mendicant! When bailed out it will float lightly. Having cut off desire and hate, you shall reach extinguishment. / Dhp 370: Five to cut, five to drop, and five more to develop. When a mendicant slips five chains they’re said to have crossed the flood. / Dhp 371: Practice absorption, don’t be negligent! Don’t let the mind delight in the senses! Don’t heedlessly swallow a hot iron ball! And when it burns, don’t cry, “Oh, the pain!” / Dhp 372: No absorption for one without wisdom, no wisdom for one without absorption. But one with absorption and wisdom— they have truly drawn near to extinguishment. / Dhp 373: A mendicant who enters an empty hut with mind at peace finds a superhuman delight as they rightly discern the Dhamma. / Dhp 374: Whenever they are mindful of the rise and fall of the aggregates, they feel rapture and joy: that is freedom from death for one who knows. / Dhp 375: This is the very start of the path for a wise mendicant here: guarding the senses, contentment, and restraint in the monastic code. / Dhp 376: Mix with spiritual friends, who are tireless and pure of livelihood. Share what you have with others, being skillful in your conduct. And when you’re full of joy, you’ll make an end to suffering.

question: In one past-life story a couple are the only survivors when their boat goes down, and they end up stranded, eating whatever the local birds lay. Which story?
title: The Story about the Elder Upananda the Sakyan
synopsis: Elder Upananda taught well, but was a greedy bhikkhu who always took the biggest offering, one day he swindled two bhikkhus out of a blanket, and the Buddha explained that one should train oneself before teaching to others, and summarised his teaching with a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 158: The astute would avoid being corrupted by first grounding themselves in what is suitable, and then instructing others.

question: In one past-life story a couple are the only survivors when their boat goes down, and they end up stranded, eating whatever the local birds lay. Which story?
title: The Story about Devadatta
synopsis: Devadatta grew jealous and plotted to kill the Buddha, when that failed he tried to cause a schism; eventually he wished to seek for forgiveness, but before he reached the Buddha he fell into Avīci, the hell of relentless suffering; the Buddha summarised the events with a verse. Sāriputta, Elder Mahā Moggallāna, Elder Kokālika
verse_english: Dhp 17: Here they’re tormented, hereafter they’re tormented, an evildoer is tormented in both places. They’re tormented thinking of bad things they’ve done; when gone to a bad place, they’re tormented all the more.

question: In one past-life story a couple are the only survivors when their boat goes down, and they end up stranded, eating whatever the local birds lay. Which story?
title: The Story about the Elder Bāhiya Dārucīriya
synopsis: Bāhiya Dārucīriya obtained a short teaching from the Buddha, became an Arahat and died straight afterwards; the Buddha appointed him as foremost amongst those who were quick to grasp the teaching, and when the bhikkhus doubted it, he taught them with a verse. Buddhas
verse_english: Dhp 101: Better than a thousand meaningless verses is a single meaningful verse, hearing which brings you peace.

question: In one past-life story a couple are the only survivors when their boat goes down, and they end up stranded, eating whatever the local birds lay. Which story?
title: The Story about the Elder Belaṭṭhisīsa
synopsis: Elder Belaṭṭhisīsa took to storing up food so as not to be bothered with the almsround; the bhikkhus reported it to the Buddha, who laid down a rule forbidding the storing of food, and gave this teaching.
verse_english: Dhp 92: Those with nothing stored up, who have understood their food, whose domain is the liberation of the signless and the empty: their path is hard to trace, like birds in the sky.

question: Why did the Buddha keep gazing at a young woman standing at the edge of the crowd with her basket?
title: The Story about the Elder Janapada Kaḷyāṇī Rūpanandā
synopsis: The Buddha caused Elder Rūpanandā, who was proud of her beauty, to see an image of a very beautiful woman quickly go through the stages of life, die, and be eaten by animals, and she gained insight into the nature of the body; the Buddha then spoke a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 150: In this city built of bones, plastered with flesh and blood, old age and death are stashed away, along with conceit and contempt.

question: Why did the Buddha keep gazing at a young woman standing at the edge of the crowd with her basket?
title: The Story about the Weaver’s Daughter
synopsis: A weaver’s daughter heard the Buddha teach on contemplation of death and undertook the practice herself; after three years the Buddha returned to her home town and asked her four questions which she sagely answered, but no one understood her answers except the Buddha; he then spoke a verse, hearing which, she attained Stream-entry.
verse_english: Dhp 174: Blind is the world, few are those who clearly see. Only a handful go to heaven, like a bird freed from a net.

question: Why did the Buddha keep gazing at a young woman standing at the edge of the crowd with her basket?
title: The Story about the Twin Miracle
synopsis: After spending his seventh Rains Retreat teaching the Abhidhamma in the Realm of the Thirty-Three, the Buddha descended on a staircase built by Sakka, the Lord of the Devas, and Elder Sāriputta praised the Buddha in his glory; the Buddha explained the matter by reciting a verse. Bimbisāra, King Pasenadi Kosala, Sakka, Gaṇḍa, Elder Ānanda, Devaputta Vātavalāhaka, Devaputta Sun, Pūraṇa Kassapa, Gharaṇī, Culla Anāthapiṇḍika, Mahā Brahma, Sāmaṇerī Cīrā, Sāmaṇera Cunda, Bhikkhunī Uppalavaṇṇā, Nandivisāla, Elder Anuruddha, Culla Anāthapiṇḍika, Deva Indaka, Deva Aṅkura, Buddha Kassapa, Deva Pañcasikha, Mātali the charioteer, Suyāma Lives, Previous Buddhas, Bodhisatta
verse_english: Dhp 181: The attentive intent on absorption, who love the peace of renunciation, the Buddhas, ever mindful, are envied by even the gods.

question: Why did the Buddha keep gazing at a young woman standing at the edge of the crowd with her basket?
title: The Story about the Edler Ānanda’s Question about the Observance Day
synopsis: Elder Ānanda asked the Buddha to explain how the previous Buddhas had kept the Observance Day; he explained that although they held them after different lengths of time, the verses they recited were always the same, and he recited them. Kakusandha, Buddha Koṇāgamana, Buddha Kassapa
verse_english: Dhp 183: Not to do any evil; to embrace the good; to purify one’s mind: this is the instruction of the Buddhas. / Dhp 184: Patient acceptance is the ultimate fervor. Extinguishment is the ultimate, say the Buddhas. No true renunciate injures another, nor does an ascetic hurt another. / Dhp 185: Not speaking ill nor doing harm; restraint in the monastic code; moderation in eating; staying in remote lodgings; commitment to the higher mind— this is the instruction of the Buddhas.

question: Why did the Buddha keep gazing at a young woman standing at the edge of the crowd with her basket?
title: The Story about a Son of a Wagon Driver
synopsis: A youth became very practised at the recollection of the Buddha, so when he was attacked by Amanussas he called out: ‘Homage to the Buddha’, which forced the Amanussas to serve him; when the king found out he asked the Buddha if only this recollection was an effective protection, and the Buddha taught six types of meditation.
verse_english: Dhp 296: The disciples of Gotama always wake up refreshed, who day and night constantly recollect the Buddha. / Dhp 297: The disciples of Gotama always wake up refreshed, who day and night constantly recollect the teaching. / Dhp 298: The disciples of Gotama always wake up refreshed, who day and night constantly recollect the Saṅgha. / Dhp 299: The disciples of Gotama always wake up refreshed, who day and night are constantly mindful of the body. / Dhp 300: The disciples of Gotama always wake up refreshed, whose minds day and night delight in harmlessness. / Dhp 301: The disciples of Gotama always wake up refreshed, whose minds day and night delight in meditation.

question: Why did the Buddha keep gazing at a young woman standing at the edge of the crowd with her basket?
title: The Story about Udena
synopsis: King Udena had two queens, Sāmāvatī, who was a follower of the Buddha, and Māgandiyā, who was spurned by the Buddha; out of jealousy Māgandiyā brought about the destruction of Sāmāvatī and her five hundred followers, all of whom had attained stages of Awakening; Māgandiyā and her family, who were full of defilements, were put to death by the king; when what had happened was reported to the Buddha he spoke some verses about them.
verse_english: Dhp 21: Heedfulness is the state free of death; heedlessness is the state of death. The heedful do not die, while the heedless are like the dead. / Dhp 22: Understanding this distinction when it comes to heedfulness, the astute rejoice in heedfulness, happy in the noble ones’ domain. / Dhp 23: They who regularly meditate, always staunchly vigorous; the attentive realize extinguishment, the supreme sanctuary from the yoke.

question: Why did the Buddha keep gazing at a young woman standing at the edge of the crowd with her basket?
title: The Story about a Certain Maiden of Family
synopsis: The Buddha and the monastics were invited to a wedding, and the bride served them with all due attention; the groom, however, was overcome with lust and could pay no attention to his duties; the Buddha spoke a verse to him.
verse_english: Dhp 202: There is no fire like greed, no crime like hate, no suffering like the aggregates, no bliss beyond peace.

question: Why did the Buddha keep gazing at a young woman standing at the edge of the crowd with her basket?
title: The Story about the Novice Sumana
synopsis: Elder Anuruddha gave the young boy Sumana the going-forth and he soon became an Arahat; through his power the novice overcame a Nāga who then became his servant; when bhikkhus who did not know who he was started making fun of the novice the Buddha decided to let him demonstrate his power and sent him to Lake Anotatta in the Himalayas to bring water; the Buddha pointed him out flying through the air and spoke a verse. the Sakyan, Mahānāma, Elder Anuruddha, Mahā Muṇḍa, Mahā Sumana, Culla Sumana, Paṇṇaka, Sakka, Suyāma, Santusita, Paranimmitavasavattī, Elder Ānanda
verse_english: Dhp 382: A young mendicant devoted to the Buddha’s teaching, lights up the world, like the moon freed from clouds.

question: A golden dish goes missing from the king's palace and turns up in a boy's wagon, with writing carved into it. What story is this from?
title: The Story about the Elder Who Meditated on a Mirage
synopsis: A bhikkhu who had been practising meditation saw a mirage, and realised this was similar to existence; he next saw froth on a river, with its bubbles bursting, and he realised existence is the same; the Buddha summed up his insight with a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 46: Knowing this body’s like foam, realizing it’s all just a mirage, and cutting off Māra’s blossoming, vanish from the King of Death.

question: A golden dish goes missing from the king's palace and turns up in a boy's wagon, with writing carved into it. What story is this from?
title: The Story about the Childless Rich Man
synopsis: In a previous life a rich man gave a meal to a Paccekabuddha but almost instantly regretted it; later, out of greed, he also killed his brother’s son; when reborn, because of his gift he was again rich, but because of his bad deed he was childless, lived as a miser and was unable to enjoy his riches; when he died all his wealth went to the king; the Buddha explained the situation with a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 355: Riches ruin a simpleton, but not a seeker of the far shore. From craving for wealth, a simpleton ruins themselves and others.

question: A golden dish goes missing from the king's palace and turns up in a boy's wagon, with writing carved into it. What story is this from?
title: The Story about the Selfish Kosiya
synopsis: Elder Moggallāna brought the miser Kosiya and his wife to the Buddha who taught them about generosity, and they both attained Stream-entry; the Buddha praised Elder Moggallāna for being both persuasive and modest with his supporters, and spoke a verse about him.
verse_english: Dhp 49: A bee takes the nectar and moves on, doing no damage to the flower’s beauty and fragrance; and that’s how a sage should walk in the village.

question: A golden dish goes missing from the king's palace and turns up in a boy's wagon, with writing carved into it. What story is this from?
title: The Story about Prince Bodhi
synopsis: Prince Bodhi invited the Buddha for the first meal in his new palace, and put down cloth thinking if the Buddha stepped on it he would be blessed with children; the Buddha refused to walk on it, and explained that Prince Bodhi would be without children because of a past life in which he failed to protect himself by keeping precepts during any of the three periods of his life, and he then gave a teaching in a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 157: If you knew your self as beloved, you’d look after it so well. In one of the night’s three watches, an astute person would remain alert.

question: A golden dish goes missing from the king's palace and turns up in a boy's wagon, with writing carved into it. What story is this from?
title: The Story about the Old Brahmin’s Sons
synopsis: Some children who were previously negligent later gave a meal to the Buddha and the Saṅgha, and related how they now took care of their father; the Buddha recited a Birth Story relating how he too had cared for his parents, and spoke a verse showing how he would not eat until he was allowed to attend to his duties.
verse_english: Dhp 324: The tusker named Dhanapāla is musky in rut, hard to control. Bound, he eats not a morsel, for he misses the elephant forest.

question: A golden dish goes missing from the king's palace and turns up in a boy's wagon, with writing carved into it. What story is this from?
title: The Story about the Elder Mahā Moggallāna
synopsis: Elder Moggallāna was murdered by brigands acting on behalf of the naked ascetics; the Buddha explained that in a past life, being swayed by his wife he had murdered his parents, which was why he died in this way in the present life, and then he spoke some verses.
verse_english: Dhp 137: One who violently attacks the peaceful and the innocent swiftly falls to one of ten bad states: / Dhp 138: harsh pain; loss; the breakup of the body; serious illness; mental distress; / Dhp 139: hazards from rulers; vicious slander; loss of kin; destruction of wealth; / Dhp 140: or else their home is consumed by fire. When their body breaks up, that witless person is reborn in hell.

question: A golden dish goes missing from the king's palace and turns up in a boy's wagon, with writing carved into it. What story is this from?
title: The Story about Devadatta
synopsis: Devadatta grew jealous and plotted to kill the Buddha, when that failed he tried to cause a schism; eventually he wished to seek for forgiveness, but before he reached the Buddha he fell into Avīci, the hell of relentless suffering; the Buddha summarised the events with a verse. Sāriputta, Elder Mahā Moggallāna, Elder Kokālika
verse_english: Dhp 17: Here they’re tormented, hereafter they’re tormented, an evildoer is tormented in both places. They’re tormented thinking of bad things they’ve done; when gone to a bad place, they’re tormented all the more.

question: A woman betrays her husband in a fight by arming his attacker, and is later deserted by that same man. Which story tells this?
title: The Story about the Elder Kuṇḍalakesī
synopsis: Kuṇḍalakesī, who had previously killed her husband and joined the wanderers and expertly defended their doctrines, was converted by Elder Sāriputta with a simple teaching; the bhikkhus wondered how, and the Buddha spoke some verses to explain it.
verse_english: Dhp 102: Better than reciting a hundred meaningless verses is a single saying of Dhamma, hearing which brings you peace. / Dhp 103: The supreme conqueror is not he who conquers a million men in battle, but he who conquers a single man: himself.

question: A woman betrays her husband in a fight by arming his attacker, and is later deserted by that same man. Which story tells this?
title: The Story about the Wise Archer Culla Dhanuggaha
synopsis: When Elder Culla Dhanuggaha obtained water from the house of a young maiden she soon started giving him porridge also and striking up a conversation, and eventually he began to feel discontent; when the Buddha heard of the situation he described how this woman murdered him at the drop of a hat in a previous existence and further gave him a teaching in a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 349: For a personage churned by thoughts, very lustful, focusing on beauty, their craving grows and grows, tying them with a stout bond. / Dhp 350: But one who loves to calm their thoughts, developing perception of ugliness, ever mindful, will surely eliminate that craving, cutting off the bonds of Māra.

question: A woman betrays her husband in a fight by arming his attacker, and is later deserted by that same man. Which story tells this?
title: The Story about a Certain Youth of Good Family
synopsis: A youth got married but his wife was given to adultery and put the young man to shame; when he met the Buddha the latter reminded him that in a previous existence also he was betrayed by his wife, and then he taught him with a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 242: Misconduct is a woman’s stain. A giver’s stain is stinginess. Bad qualities are a stain in this world and the next. / Dhp 243: But a worse stain than these is ignorance, the worst stain of all. Having given up that stain, be without stains, mendicants!

question: A woman betrays her husband in a fight by arming his attacker, and is later deserted by that same man. Which story tells this?
title: The Story about the Woman Jealous by Nature
synopsis: A jealous woman found out her husband had been unfaithful with one of their maidservants, and had her nose and ears cut off, threw her into a dungeon and then went to listen to the Dhamma; one of her relatives discovered the matter and informed the Buddha, who gave the teaching in a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 314: A bad deed is better left undone, for it will plague you later on. A good deed is better done, one that does not plague you.

question: A woman betrays her husband in a fight by arming his attacker, and is later deserted by that same man. Which story tells this?
title: The Story about Three Groups
synopsis: Three different groups of bhikkhus who were on their way to the Buddha saw a crow die in mid-air, a woman drowned on a voyage and themselves get buried in a cave; they asked the Buddha why it all happened, and he explained there is nowhere to escape from the results of bad actions, and spoke a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 127: Not in midair, nor mid-ocean, nor hiding in a mountain cleft; you’ll find no place on the planet to escape your wicked deeds.

question: A woman betrays her husband in a fight by arming his attacker, and is later deserted by that same man. Which story tells this?
title: The Story about Khema
synopsis: One of the merchant Anāthapiṇḍika’s nephews, Khema, was so handsome all the women fell in love with him, and he was frequently caught in adultery; the king didn’t punish Khema, due to his affection for his father, so his father took his son to the Buddha who taught him in some verses the destiny of those who dally with other men’s wives.
verse_english: Dhp 309: Four things befall a heedless man who sleeps with another’s wife: wickedness, poor sleep, ill-repute, and rebirth in hell. / Dhp 310: He accrues wickedness and is reborn in a bad place, all so a frightened couple may snatch a moment’s pleasure, for which rulers impose a heavy punishment. That’s why a man should not sleep with another’s wife.

question: A woman betrays her husband in a fight by arming his attacker, and is later deserted by that same man. Which story tells this?
title: The Story about a Certain Bhikkhu
synopsis: A bhikkhu was given a subject of meditation, went to the forest, and became an Arahat; as he was travelling a woman who had quarrelled with her husband followed close behind; when the husband saw them he thrashed the bhikkhu; the bhikkhus could not believe he had not got angry with the man, but the Buddha confirmed his purity with a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 405: They’ve laid aside violence against creatures firm and frail; not killing or making others kill: that’s who I declare a brahmin.

question: A woman betrays her husband in a fight by arming his attacker, and is later deserted by that same man. Which story tells this?
title: The Story about the Defeat of the King of Kosala
synopsis: The King of Kosala is defeated three times by his nephew Ajātasattu, the King of Magadha, and took to his bed in sorrow and despair; when the Buddha heard about it he gave this teaching.
verse_english: Dhp 201: Victory breeds enmity; the defeated sleep badly. The peaceful sleep at ease, having left victory and defeat behind.

question: In which story does a parrot refuse to leave a dead fig tree out of loyalty, and Sakka comes in disguise to test it?
title: The Story about Devadatta
synopsis: Devadatta sought to kill the Buddha and take over the running of the Saṅgha; the Buddha explained that he also tried to kill him in other existences, but it all worked to Devadatta’s downfall, and then he spoke a verse about him.
verse_english: Dhp 162: One choked by immorality, as a sal tree by a creeper, does to themselves what a foe only wishes.

question: In which story does a parrot refuse to leave a dead fig tree out of loyalty, and Sakka comes in disguise to test it?
title: The Story about the Elder Nigamavāsī Tissa
synopsis: Nigamavāsī Tissa lived near Sāvatthī and after he ordained he only went to his local village for alms; the bhikkhus blamed him but the Buddha praised him for being frugal and content, and spoke a verse praising his way of life.
verse_english: Dhp 32: A mendicant who loves diligence, seeing fear in negligence— such a one can’t decline, and has drawn near to extinguishment.

question: In which story does a parrot refuse to leave a dead fig tree out of loyalty, and Sakka comes in disguise to test it?
title: The Story about a Discontented Bhikkhu
synopsis: A bhikkhu had gained an inheritance of one hundred coins from his father and thought to return to the lay life; the Buddha pointed out that the money would not be enough to support himself, and related the Birth Story about Mandhātā which shows that no matter how much a person has he will never be satisfied.
verse_english: Dhp 186: Even if it were raining money, you’d not be sated in sensual pleasures. An astute person understands that sensual pleasures offer little gratification and much suffering. / Dhp 187: Thus they find no delight even in celestial pleasures. A disciple of the fully awakened Buddha delights in the ending of craving.

question: In which story does a parrot refuse to leave a dead fig tree out of loyalty, and Sakka comes in disguise to test it?
title: The Story about Mahāli’s Questions
synopsis: Prince Magha did good works in his village and inspired thirty-three others to join him; later they were reborn as Sakka and his company of Thirty-three; the Buddha spoke a verse explaining what had happened.
verse_english: Dhp 30: Maghavā became chief of the gods by means of diligence. People praise diligence, while negligence is always deplored.

question: In which story does a parrot refuse to leave a dead fig tree out of loyalty, and Sakka comes in disguise to test it?
title: The Story about Giving Alms to the Elder Mahā Kassapa
synopsis: Elder Mahā Kassapa rose from meditation after seven days and went for alms; celestial spirits stepped forward to donate to him but he dismissed them, then Sakka and his wife Sujā disguised themselves as weavers and succeeded in giving alms, but Elder Mahā Kassapa discovered who they were and chided them; the Buddha spoke a verse about him.
verse_english: Dhp 56: Faint is the fragrance of sandal or pinwheel; but the fragrance of the virtuous floats to the highest gods.

question: In which story does a parrot refuse to leave a dead fig tree out of loyalty, and Sakka comes in disguise to test it?
title: The Story about the Novice Paṇḍita
synopsis: The novice Paṇḍita saw that irrigators, fletchers and carpenters mastered the objects they worked with, and realised that if they can master unconscious things, he could master his mind; by striving he did just that and became an Arahat; the Buddha then spoke a verse about him. Sāriputta
verse_english: Dhp 80: While irrigators guide water, fletchers bend arrows straight, and carpenters bend timber straight, the astute tame themselves.

question: Whose wife called after him, with her hair only half combed, asking him to come back soon, which later made him want to leave the monastery?
title: The Story about Kosambivāsī Tissa’s Novice
synopsis: Elder Tissa ordained a novice, who in the ordination hall became an Arahat; later they travelled, and through the carelessness of the bhikkhu the novice’s eye was put out; the novice, however, didn’t get angry but went about his duties as normal; the Buddha explained it with a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 96: Their mind is peaceful, peaceful are their speech and deeds. Such a one is at peace, rightly freed through enlightenment.

question: Whose wife called after him, with her hair only half combed, asking him to come back soon, which later made him want to leave the monastery?
title: The Story about the Elder Cittahattha
synopsis: Cittahattha wavered continually between being a bhikkhu and a householder, but eventually he saw into the truth of impermanence, ordained yet again and became an Arahat; the Buddha spoke some verses about him.
verse_english: Dhp 38: Those of unsteady mind, who don’t understand the true teaching, and whose confidence wavers, do not perfect their wisdom. / Dhp 39: One whose mind is not festering, whose heart is undamaged, who’s given up right and wrong, alert, has nothing to fear.

question: Whose wife called after him, with her hair only half combed, asking him to come back soon, which later made him want to leave the monastery?
title: The Story about a Company of Bhikkhus
synopsis: After Soṇa Kūṭikaṇṇa received ordination he recited Dhamma to the Buddha who praised him for it, which also caused the Devas to rejoice; on hearing about it, Soṇa’s mother invited her son to teach her Dhamma also, and wouldn’t leave the teaching even when she heard nine hundred thieves had broken into her house; seeing her piety, the thieves converted and went forth; this is the teaching the Buddha gave at that time.
verse_english: Dhp 368: A mendicant who meditates on love, devoted to the Buddha’s teaching, would realize the peaceful state, the blissful stilling of conditions. / Dhp 369: Bail out this boat, mendicant! When bailed out it will float lightly. Having cut off desire and hate, you shall reach extinguishment. / Dhp 370: Five to cut, five to drop, and five more to develop. question: Santatimahamattavatthu summary
title: The Story about Settling a Dispute amongst Relatives
synopsis: The Sākiyans and the Koliyans were kindred tribes who nearly fell into a war over short water supplies; the Buddha, in order to prevent bloodshed, went to them and gave them this teaching, following which they relented.
verse_english: Dhp 197: Let us live so very happily, loving among the hostile. Among hostile humans, let us live with love. / Dhp 198: Let us live so very happily, healthy among the ailing. Among ailing humans let us live healthily. / Dhp 199: Let us live so very happily, content among the greedy. Among greedy humans, let us live content.

question: Santatimahamattavatthu summary
title: The Story about Kukkuṭamitta
synopsis: The Buddha taught Kukkuṭamitta the hunter, his seven sons and seven daughters, and they all gained Stream-entry; the Buddha also explained that the hunter’s wife attained Stream-entry while still young; the bhikkhus asked how can anyone who has Stream-entry help a hunter, and the Buddha explained the matter with a verse. Buddhas
verse_english: Dhp 124: You can carry poison in your hand if it has no wound, for poison does not infect without a wound; nothing bad happens unless you do bad.

question: Santatimahamattavatthu summary
title: The Story about the Elder Naṅgalakula
synopsis: The poor man Naṅgalakula was ordained, but became discontented, and thought to return to the lay life; but finding his previous rags he took them as a meditation subject and soon became an Arahat; the Buddha confirmed it to the bhikkhus and spoke some verses.
verse_english: Dhp 379: Urge yourself on, reflect on yourself. A mendicant self-controlled and mindful will always dwell in happiness. / Dhp 380: Self is indeed the lord of self, for who else would be one’s lord? Self is indeed the home of self, so restrain yourself, as a merchant his thoroughbred steed.

question: Santatimahamattavatthu summary
title: The Story about the Elder Ānanda
synopsis: One day Elder Ānanda saw the sun set, the moon rise, the king in his mantle, Elder Kāḷudāyi meditating and the Buddha, who outshone them all; the Teacher explained that Buddhas outshine the others both by day and by night, and spoke a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 387: The sun blazes by day, the moon radiates at night, the aristocrat shines in armor, and the brahmin shines in absorption. But all day and all night, the Buddha blazes with glory.

question: Santatimahamattavatthu summary
title: The Story about Kumbhaghosaka
synopsis: Kumbhaghosaka was a rich man’s son who escaped his afflicted household during a plague; later he disguised himself as a poor man and worked for his living, but was recognised by the king, who honoured him and gave him his daughter in marriage; when he heard the story the Buddha spoke a verse about him.
verse_english: Dhp 24: For the hard-working and mindful, pure of deed and attentive, restrained, living righteously, and diligent, their reputation only grows.

question: Kokasunakhaluddakavatthu
title: The Story about Kokālika
synopsis: Elder Kokālika once spent the Rains Retreat with the two Chief Disciples, but was not honoured as they were, and then went about abusing them, saying they were full of defilements; the Buddha tried to restrain him but he fell into the Lotus Niraya Hell; the Buddha then explained how a bhikkhu should behave with a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 363: When a mendicant of restrained mouth, thoughtful in counsel, not restless, explains the text and its meaning, their words are sweet.

question: Kokasunakhaluddakavatthu
title: The Story about the Hunter Koka’s Dogs
synopsis: The hunter Koka blamed a bhikkhu for his failure to catch game and he set his dogs on him, chasing him up a tree; the bhikkhu’s robe fell over the hunter and the dogs mistakenly devoured him instead; the bhikkhu worried whether his actions led to the death of the man, and the Buddha reassured him with a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 125: Whoever wrongs a man who has done no wrong, a pure man who has not a blemish, the evil backfires on the fool, like fine dust thrown upwind.

question: Kokasunakhaluddakavatthu
title: The Story about Devadatta
synopsis: Elder Sāriputta taught on generosity and people decided to give alms; one man gave a robe, which they decided to give to Elder Devadatta; when the Buddha heard about it he related a Birth Story about Devadatta, who, as an elephant hunter, disguised himself as a Paccekabuddha in order to kill his prey, and then spoke some verses about him.
verse_english: Dhp 9: One who, not free of stains themselves, would wear the robe stained in ocher, bereft of self-control and truth: they are not worthy of the ocher robe. / Dhp 10: One who’s purged all their stains, steady in ethics, possessed of self-control and of truth, they are truly worthy of the ocher robe.

question: Kokasunakhaluddakavatthu
title: The Story about the Elder Uppalavaṇṇā
synopsis: After the rape of Elder Uppalavaṇṇā the bhikkhus were discussing whether those who had become an Arahat still enjoyed the pleasures of the flesh; when this was reported to the Buddha he said it was not so, and – affirming her purity of mind – he spoke a verse explaining the situation.
verse_english: Dhp 401: Like water from a lotus leaf, like a mustard seed off the point of a pin, sensual pleasures slip off them: that’s who I declare a brahmin.

question: Kokasunakhaluddakavatthu
title: The Story about Five Hundred Youths
synopsis: Fifty youths were going out of Rājagaha carrying baskets of cakes, but did not think to offer any to the Buddha and the bhikkhus, until they saw Elder Mahā Kassapa, and then they offered him the cakes; the Buddha spoke a verse about Elder Mahā Kassapa.
verse_english: Dhp 217: One accomplished in virtue and vision, firmly principled, and truthful, doing oneself what ought be done: that’s who the people love.

question: Kokasunakhaluddakavatthu
title: The Story about Pasedani Kosala
synopsis: King Pasenadi was always overeating and suffering for it so the Buddha had the king’s nephew learn and recite a verse which reminded the king to be moderate; later the king told the Buddha he was cured, and the Buddha recited a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 204: Health is the ultimate blessing; contentment, the ultimate wealth; trust is the ultimate family; extinguishment, the ultimate happiness.

question: Kokasunakhaluddakavatthu
title: The Story about Pasenadi Kosala
synopsis: King Pasenadi, at one time in his life, always overate and suffered the consequences of torpidity and drowsiness; he went to the Buddha who taught him with a verse; he also taught another verse for his attendant to recite which would remind the king not to eat so much.
verse_english: Dhp 325: One who gets drowsy from overeating, fond of sleep, rolling round the bed like a great hog stuffed with grain: that dullard returns to the womb again and again.

question: Kokasunakhaluddakavatthu
title: The Story about Those from Kosambī
synopsis: Parallels: Ja 428; Vin Mv 10.1-5; Ud 4.5; Ja 37124 The followers of two bhikkhus of Kosambī fell into a dispute and despite the Buddha’s admonitions, refused to be reconciled; the Buddha went forth to Pārileyyaka forest and was served by an elephant and a monkey; meanwhile the lay people refused to attend on the bhikkhus till they came to their senses; eventually they asked for forgiveness and the Buddha taught them with a verse. Kosala, Prince Dīghāvu, Bālaka, Elder Bhagu, Anāthapiṇḍika, Visākhā
verse_english: Dhp 6: When others do not understand, let us, who do understand this, restrain ourselves in this regard; for that is how conflicts are laid to rest.

question: Kokasunakhaluddakavatthu
title: The Story about Culla Sāri
synopsis: Elder Culla Sāri gave medical treatment to others in exchange for a portion of food, which is against the right ways of earning his livelihood as laid down by the Buddha; when the Buddha heard of his behaviour he gave a teaching in some verses.
verse_english: Dhp 244: Life is easy for the shameless. With all the rude courage of a crow, they live pushy, rude, and corrupt. / Dhp 245: Life is hard for the conscientious, always seeking purity, neither clinging nor rude, pure of livelihood and discerning.

question: What did the Buddha teach Sāriputta's nephew about reaching the Brahma world?
title: The Story about the Novice Saṅkicca
synopsis: CST4 & PTS Saṁkiccasāmaṇeravatthu Elder Sāriputta’s nephew Saṅkicca ordained as a novice, and when thirty bhikkhus’ lives were threatened by five hundred thieves he converted the thieves and they ordained; when he heard about it, this is the teaching the Buddha gave.
verse_english: Dhp 110: Better to live a single day ethical and absorbed in meditation than to live a hundred years unethical and lacking immersion.

question: What did the Buddha teach Sāriputta's nephew about reaching the Brahma world?
title: The Story about the Elder Sāriputta’s Brahmin Uncle
synopsis: Elder Sāriputta asked the Buddha to teach his uncle, who supported the Nigaṇṭhas, the true way to the Brahma world; and the Buddha spoke a verse with which he taught them.

title: The Story about the Novice Sumana
synopsis: Elder Anuruddha gave the young boy Sumana the going-forth and he soon became an Arahat; through his power the novice overcame a Nāga who then became his servant; when bhikkhus who did not know who he was started making fun of the novice the Buddha decided to let him demonstrate his power and sent him to Lake Anotatta in the Himalayas to bring water; the Buddha pointed him out flying through the air and spoke a verse. the Sakyan, Mahānāma, Elder Anuruddha, Mahā Muṇḍa, Mahā Sumana, Culla Sumana, Paṇṇaka, Sakka, Suyāma, Santusita, Paranimmitavasavattī, Elder Ānanda
verse_english: Dhp 382: A young mendicant devoted to the Buddha’s teaching, lights up the world, like the moon freed from clouds.

verse_english: Dhp 384: When a brahmin has gone beyond dualistic phenomena, then they consciously make an end of all fetters.

verse_english: Dhp 225: Those harmless sages, always restrained in body, go to the state that does not pass, where there is no sorrow.

synopsis: Elder Sappadāsa was dissatisfied and thought to end his life, but became an Arahat with the razor at his windpipe; when questioned by the bhikkhus the Buddha explained that one who truly strives can attain Awakening in an instant, and he spoke a verse. Elder Sappadāsa, Buddha Kassapa
verse_english: Dhp 112: Better to live a single day energetic and strong, than to live a hundred years lazy and lacking energy.

title: The Story about the Bhikkhus of Bhaddiya

verse_english: Dhp 292: They dump what should be done, and do what should not be done. For the insolent and the negligent, their defilements only grow. / Dhp 293: Those that have properly undertaken constant mindfulness of the body, don’t cultivate what should not be done, but always do what should be done. question: Which stories are about monks who decided to take their own lives?

question: Which stories are about monks who decided to take their own lives?
title: The Story about a Certain Man
synopsis: King Pasenadi was overcome with desire for another man’s wife and sought to have him killed; during the night he woke to the sound of four people screaming; the Buddha explained they were adulterers in their previous lives and did no good deeds, and then he spoke a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 60: Long is the night for the wakeful; long is the league for the weary; long transmigrate the fools who don’t understand the true teaching.

question: Which stories are about monks who decided to take their own lives?
title: The Story about the Elder Godhika’s Parinibbāna
synopsis: Gravely ill, Elder Godhika kept falling away from his concentration and decided to commit suicide; after the event Māra searched high and low for his place of rebirth, but the Buddha asserted that he had not been reborn, and spoke a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 57: For those accomplished in ethics, meditating diligently, freed through the highest knowledge, Māra cannot find their path.

question: Which stories are about monks who decided to take their own lives?
title: The Story about the Fruits and Powers of People’s Bad Conduct
synopsis: Elder Moggallāna saw a Peta dressed as a bhikkhu flying through the air with body all on fire and reported it to the Buddha, who told that previously the Peta had been a bhikkhu under Buddha Kassapa, but had not lived accordingly, and then he spoke a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 307: Many who wear a scrap of ocher cloth are unrestrained and wicked. Being wicked, they are reborn in hell due to their bad deeds.

question: Which stories are about monks who decided to take their own lives?
title: The Story about the Five Hundred Bhikkhus
synopsis: Five hundred bhikkhus who had received instructions from the Buddha saw jasmine flowers fading away and determined to attain Awakening before the flowers dropped from the stems; the Buddha projected an image of himself and gave them this teaching, after hearing which, they became Arahats.
verse_english: Dhp 377: As a jasmine sheds its withered flowers, O mendicants, shed greed and hate.

question: Which stories tell of a chief disciple leaving a rains retreat and asking for the requisites to be sent on?

synopsis: While the Buddha and his disciples were on walking tour they came to the shrine of Kassapa, a previous Buddha; one Brahmin came and paid homage to the shrine, but not to the Buddha or his disciples; the Buddha lauded the Brahmin for his act of faith but said it is even better to worship those still living who are worthy of worship.

question: Which stories tell of a chief disciple leaving a rains retreat and asking for the requisites to be sent on?
title: The Story about Kokālika
synopsis: Elder Kokālika once spent the Rains Retreat with the two Chief Disciples, but was not honoured as they were, and then went about abusing them, saying they were full of defilements; the Buddha tried to restrain him but he fell into the Lotus Niraya Hell; the Buddha then explained how a bhikkhu should behave with a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 363: When a mendicant of restrained mouth, thoughtful in counsel, not restless, explains the text and its meaning, their words are sweet.

question: Which stories tell of a chief disciple leaving a rains retreat and asking for the requisites to be sent on?
title: The Story about the Elder Pabbhāravāsī Tissa
synopsis: Elder Pabbhāravāsī Tissa went forth to a certain rock cave in order to forward his meditation; the deity residing there moved out and tried to slander the elder; recalling his own virtue, however, the elder soon became an Arahat; the bhikkhus could not believe he had not got angry with the deity, but the Buddha confirmed his purity with a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 404: Mixing with neither householders nor the homeless; a migrant with no bastion, few in wishes: that’s who I declare a brahmin.

question: Which stories tell of a chief disciple leaving a rains retreat and asking for the requisites to be sent on?
title: The Story about the Elder Sāriputta
synopsis: After Elder Sāriputta had spent the Rains Retreat with five hundred bhikkhus the lay people still hadn’t donated the requisites; as he was leaving he asked for the requisites to be sent on, or that he be told; the bhikkhus reported it to the Buddha who explained it was concern for the donors and the young bhikkhus that made him ask so, and not craving, and then spoke a verse about the one without craving.
verse_english: Dhp 410: They have no hope in this world or the next; with no need for hope, detached: that’s who I declare a brahmin.

question: Which stories tell of a chief disciple leaving a rains retreat and asking for the requisites to be sent on?
title: The Story about the Elder Vanavāsī Tissa
synopsis: The seven year old boy Tissa ordained under Elder Sāriputta, and later, spurning gains and the attentions of his relatives, went forth into solitude, and quickly became an Arahat; the Buddha spoke a verse about him. (Piṇḍapātadāyaka Tissa, Kambaladāyaka Tissa), Brahmin Mahāsena, Elder Sāriputta, Elder Mahā Moggallāna, Upasāḷhaka, Elder Ānanda
verse_english: Dhp 75: For the means to profit and the path to quenching are two quite different things. A mendicant disciple of the Buddha, understanding what this really means, would never delight in honors, but rather would foster seclusion.

question: Which stories tell of a chief disciple leaving a rains retreat and asking for the requisites to be sent on?
title: The Story about the Elder Mahā Moggallāna
synopsis: After Elder Moggallāna had spent the Rains Retreat with five hundred bhikkhus the lay people still hadn’t donated the requisites; as he was leaving he asked for the requisites to be sent on, or that he be told; the bhikkhus reported it to the Buddha who explained it was concern for the donors and the young bhikkhus that made him ask so, and not craving, and then spoke a verse about the one without craving.
verse_english: Dhp 411: They have no clinging, knowledge has freed them of indecision, they’ve arrived at the objective, freedom from death: that’s who I declare a brahmin.

question: Which stories tell of a chief disciple leaving a rains retreat and asking for the requisites to be sent on?
title: The Story about Garahadinna
synopsis: Sirigutta supported the Buddha, but his friend Garahadinna supported the Nigaṇṭhas; Sirigutta proved that the Nigaṇṭhas do not know the past, present and future as they declared; and the Buddha proved his knowledge and power to Garahadinna, who became his disciple; then the Buddha spoke some verses. verse_english: Dhp 58: From a heap of trash discarded on the highway, a lotus might blossom, fragrant and delightful. / Dhp 59: So too, among those thought of as trash, a disciple of the perfect Buddha outshines with their wisdom the blind ordinary folk.

question: Which stories have Sāriputta asking the Buddha to show his relatives or friends the way to the Brahma world?
title: The Story about the Elder Sāriputta’s Brahmin Uncle
synopsis: Elder Sāriputta asked the Buddha to teach his uncle, who supported the Nigaṇṭhas, the true way to the Brahma world; and the Buddha spoke a verse with which he taught them.
verse_english: Dhp 106: Rather than a thousandfold sacrifice, every month for a full century, it’s better to honor for a single hour one who has developed themselves. That offering is better than the hundred year sacrifice.

question: Which stories have Sāriputta asking the Buddha to show his relatives or friends the way to the Brahma world?
title: The Story about the Elder Sāriputta’s Brahmin Companion
synopsis: Elder Sāriputta asked the Buddha to teach his friend, who offered animals in sacrifice, the true way to the Brahma world, and the Buddha gave him a teaching in a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 108: Whatever sacrifice or offering in the world a seeker of merit may make for a year, none of it is worth a quarter of bowing to the sincere.

question: Which stories have Sāriputta asking the Buddha to show his relatives or friends the way to the Brahma world?
title: The Story about the Brahmin Devahita
synopsis: When the Buddha was ill one time he asked for hot water from the Brahmin Devahita, who readily gave it; the Brahmin then asked to whom alms were best given, and the Buddha explained that his alms had great fruit, and then spoke the following verse about the true Brahmin.
verse_english: Dhp 423: One who knows their past lives, sees heaven and places of loss, and has attained the end of rebirth; a sage of perfect insight at the summit of spiritual perfection: that’s who I declare a brahmin. The Sayings of the Dhamma are complete.

question: Which stories have Sāriputta asking the Buddha to show his relatives or friends the way to the Brahma world?
title: The Story about the Elder Sāriputta’s Nephew
synopsis: Elder Sāriputta asked the Buddha to teach his nephew, who slayed animals and tended the sacrificial fire, the true way to the Brahma world, and the Buddha gave a teaching in a verse.
verse_english: Dhp 107: Rather than serve the sacred flame in the forest for a hundred years, it’s better to honor for a single hour a personage who has developed themselves. That offering is better than the hundred year sacrifice.

question: Which stories feature hunters?
title: The Story about Kukkuṭamitta
synopsis: The Buddha taught Kukkuṭamitta the hunter, his seven sons and seven daughters, and they all gained Stream-entry; the Buddha also explained that the hunter’s wife attained Stream-entry while still young; the bhikkhus asked how can anyone who has Stream-entry help a hunter, and the Buddha explained the matter with a verse. Buddhas

verse_english: Dhp 80: While irrigators guide water, fletchers bend arrows straight, and carpenters bend timber straight, the astute tame themselves.

verse_english: Dhp 287: As a mighty flood sweeps away a sleeping village, death steals away a man who dotes on children and cattle, his mind caught up in them.

synopsis: King Udena had two queens, Sāmāvatī, who was a follower of the Buddha, and Māgandiyā, who was spurned by the Buddha; out of jealousy Māgandiyā brought about the destruction of Sāmāvatī and her five hundred followers, all of whom had attained stages of Awakening; Māgandiyā and her family, who were full of defilements, were put to death by the king; when what had happened was reported to the Buddha he spoke some verses about them.
verse_english: Dhp 21: Heedfulness is the state free of death; heedlessness is the state of death. verse_english: Dhp 203: Hunger is the worst illness, conditions are the worst suffering. When one has known this as it is, extinguishment is the ultimate happiness.

verse_english: Dhp 290: If by giving up material happiness one sees abundant happiness, the attentive would give up material happiness, seeing the abundant happiness.

verse_english: Dhp 90: At journey’s end, rid of sorrow; everywhere free, all ties given up, no fever is found in them.
